en.headline: Hong Kong Post warns public of fake websites and messages
en.dek: The postal service said on Monday it had referred to police fake websites and messages impersonating it that ask recipients for personal data or postage payments.
body: Hong Kong Post on Monday urged the public to stay alert to fraudulent websites and to SMS or email messages that claim to be from the postal service and contain links asking for personal information or postage fees.

The department said it had no connection with the fake sites and had referred the matter to the police. It reminded the public that its official websites are hongkongpost.hk, hongkongpost.gov.hk and ecert.gov.hk.

Hong Kong Post added that it only sends SMS to local mobile users under the sender name #HKPost, and emails only from the domains @hkpo.gov.hk or @hongkongpost.hk. It does not send links by email, SMS or social media to collect payments or personal data.
Members of the public with enquiries can call the Hong Kong Post enquiry hotline 2921 2222 or email hkpo@hkpo.gov.hk.

zh.headline: 香港郵政呼籲慎防偽冒網站及短訊
zh.dek: 香港郵政周一表示，已將冒認其名義的虛假網站及要求提供個人資料或支付郵費的短訊電郵轉交警方，並提醒市民官方網站及發送人名稱。
body: 香港郵政周一呼籲市民提高警覺，留意偽冒虛假網址，以及冒認香港郵政發出的虛假短訊或電郵，當中附有超連結要求收件人提供個人資料或支付郵費。
郵政署澄清與有關虛假網站並無關係，並已將事件轉交警方處理。它提醒市民，官方網站為hongkongpost.hk、hongkongpost.gov.hk及ecert.gov.hk。
香港郵政強調，只會以「#HKPost」名稱向本地流動電話用戶發出短訊，電郵則只會使用@hkpo.gov.hk或@hongkongpost.hk域名。它重申不會透過電郵、短訊或社交媒體發送超連結以收取款項及收集個人資料。
市民如有查詢，可致電香港郵政查詢熱線2921 2222或電郵至hkpo@hkpo.gov.hk。
